claude_only.name: Which authoritative master-system identifier designates this agent, and which system issues it?
Which alternate or protocol-scoped identifiers resolve to this same agent?
How is a durable agent definition distinguished from a transient in-memory agent instance?
What versioning scheme identifies a released agent definition, and which changes force a new version?
From which instant is each agent version effective, and when was it superseded?
Which fields are frozen at release so that a version identifier always denotes the same behaviour contract?
Which prior agent version was this version derived from?
What level of autonomy is the agent authorised to exercise without a human decision point?
Which architectural archetype does the agent implement: single actor, orchestrator, sub-agent or scripted workflow?
Can the agent initiate activity without a human or upstream request, and under which trigger conditions?
How often is the assigned autonomy level re-justified against observed behaviour?
Is the operator of this agent a provider or a deployer in each jurisdiction where it operates?
Which regulatory risk tier and use-case category does the agent fall into?
Which disclosure duties apply when the agent interacts with natural persons or emits synthetic content?
What evidence supports the assigned risk classification, and who signed it off?
Which model or models does the agent invoke, and are those bindings pinned or floating?
Which configuration artefact governs the agent's instructions, and at which version?
Which sub-agents or delegate agents may this agent instantiate or call?
What happens to the agent's identity and approvals when a bound component is substituted?
Which party authored and which party approved this agent definition?
From which template, framework or upstream agent definition was this definition derived?
How is responsibility for the agent's outputs attributed back to a responsible party?
How is the provenance record protected against later undetected modification?
Which tools, functions and data resources is the agent bound to, and from which servers or providers?
Which bound tools are read-only and which cause irreversible or externally visible effects?
How is each tool provider vetted, and are tool descriptions treated as untrusted content?
How is a change to a bound tool's schema, description or endpoint detected and re-approved?
Which skills or task types does the agent declare that it can perform?
Which requests must the agent refuse or route elsewhere?
What evidence shows the agent performs each declared skill at the stated quality?
Which agent and tool protocols, at which revisions, does the agent speak on each endpoint?
How does the agent negotiate protocol revisions and behave when no mutually supported revision exists?
How can a consumer verify that a published capability descriptor genuinely belongs to this agent?
Which conformance claims are asserted, and what test evidence supports them?
On whose behalf is the agent acting for a given activity, and how is that principal identified?
What is the full delegation chain from the originating human principal to this agent and its sub-agents?
Which authorities may never be sub-delegated onward to another agent?
For how long and under which conditions does a delegation remain valid?
Which credentials, tokens or keys can the agent present, and who issued each?
How is each token bound to its intended resource audience, and is pass-through forbidden?
What is the minimum scope set required for each declared skill?
How are agent credentials rotated, revoked and re-issued?
Which policy decision point authorises each agent action, and is the decision made per request?
Which actions, targets or environments are categorically forbidden to the agent?
What is the maximum blast radius of a single authorised action, and how is it bounded?
How is an emergency deviation from policy requested, approved and recorded?
Which operations require explicit user consent before the agent may proceed?
What is recorded to evidence that consent or approval was given, by whom and when?
Does a granted approval cover a single action, a session or a standing authorisation?
How is the oversight interface protected against approval fatigue and rubber-stamping?
Which named organisation and role is accountable for this agent in production?
How are build, approval and operation duties separated across roles?
Who is contactable, and within what response time, when the agent misbehaves?
What happens to accountability when the owning team, vendor or contract changes?
Which memory stores does the agent read from and write to, and what is each store's scope?
Which memory persists beyond a session, and in which storage locality is it held?
How is memory isolated between tenants, users and sessions?
When stored memory conflicts with current instructions or retrieved context, which source prevails?
What is permitted to write into durable agent memory, and under whose authority?
For each memory item, what records its origin, observation time and confidence?
Which controls detect and contain poisoned or adversarially injected memory?
How is an incorrect memory item corrected, quarantined or rolled back?
For which declared purposes may each data category be used, and what use is forbidden?
Under which conditions may data leave a jurisdiction, tenant or trust boundary?
How is it verified that the agent requests only the data it needs?
How long is each class of agent record, log and memory retained, and from which clock does the period run?
Which events trigger deletion, and how is deletion verified across replicas and backups?
How does a legal hold or open investigation suspend normal deletion?
How are conflicting duties resolved between audit retention and erasure rights?
Which lifecycle states may an agent occupy, and which transitions between them are legal?
What must be true before an agent may move into an active production state?
Which conditions force immediate suspension or withdrawal of the agent?
What must be preserved, migrated or destroyed when the agent is retired?
Which approval gates must be passed before an agent version reaches production?
Which changes count as material and therefore require re-approval?
How quickly can a released agent version be rolled back, and to which known-good state?
What record proves who approved a release, on what evidence and at what time?
Which interface affordances let a competent person understand, monitor and interrupt the agent while it is in use?
How is the agent stopped mid-task, and what state does a stop leave behind?
How does the oversight design counter automation bias and over-reliance on agent output?
What is recorded when a human overrides, corrects or halts the agent?
What limits cap the agent's steps, tool calls, recursion depth and wall-clock time per task?
Which token, compute and monetary budgets apply, and what happens when they are exhausted?
How many concurrent tasks and sessions may the agent hold, and how is contention resolved?
What is the defined behaviour on limit breach: halt, degrade or escalate?
How does an execution record reference the exact agent version that produced it?
Which correlation identifiers tie messages, tool calls and sub-agent activity into one task?
How are event time and observation or ingestion time recorded separately for agent activity?
What must be captured so that an agent activity can be reconstructed later?
Which capability, safety and robustness evaluations were run against this agent version?
Which acceptance thresholds must be met for release, and who set them?
How well does the evaluation set represent the intended operating context?
When was each evaluation run, on which version, and by whom?
Which live indicators show that the agent is still performing within its accepted envelope?
How is behavioural drift caused by model, tool or data change detected?
What proportion of agent activity is sampled for human quality review, and how is the sample selected?
What is the defined response when a monitored indicator crosses its alert threshold?
Which telemetry attribute schema is emitted for agent invocations and tool executions?
Which events must be logged so that agent activity remains traceable for its whole lifetime?
Which message content may be recorded in telemetry, and how is sensitive content redacted?
How are logs protected from tampering, and for how long are they kept?
What counts as an agent incident, near miss or serious malfunction?
To whom and within what deadline must an incident be reported?
Which containment actions are pre-authorised without further approval?
How does an incident feed back into agent policy, limits or classification?
Which agent-specific threats has this deployment been assessed against?
Which residual risks are accepted, by whom, and with what compensating controls?
Which documentation set demonstrates alignment to the applicable framework or regulation?
When was the risk assessment last refreshed, and what triggers a re-assessment?

grok_only.name: What authoritative master-system identifier does the home Agent Management System or adopting platform assign to this agent?
Under which equality rule are two agent records treated as the same actor, and is the primary name immutable for the agent's lifetime?
What governed global IRI, well-known locator or Dimension UUID/ULID is recorded when no platform AID is available or when cross-domain discovery is required?
Where is this agent's discovery manifest published, and which protocol bindings, tenants and protocol versions does it advertise?
Does the agent offer an authenticated extended discovery card, and which additional skills or interfaces appear only after authentication?
Which optional interaction capabilities (streaming, push notifications, extensions) does the agent declare, and how are undeclared capabilities rejected?
Does this actor meet the ISO/IEC 22989 definition of an AI agent, and if not, which neighbouring concept (AI system, AI component, non-agent software) applies?
What declared autonomy band does this agent operate in, relative to varying autonomy in the EU AI Act definition and any human denial rights over tool use?
Is this agent an application actor or a reserved platform service such as AMS or DF, and which reserved AID pattern does it use?
What standing goals and in-scope objectives is this agent authorised to pursue?
Which objectives are explicitly out of scope, and which stop or success criteria terminate pursuit of a goal?
Who may change the agent's goal set, and what evidence is required before a goal mutation is accepted?
On whose behalf may this agent act, and what mandate or permission scopes are delegated to it?
Which quantitative or categorical limits bound the agent's autonomous actions, including tool classes it may never invoke?
Which operations require prior human consent or allow in-loop denial, and what happens if the human is unavailable?
When was the current mandate granted, last reviewed, suspended or revoked, and at what observation time was that recorded?
Which standing policy packs, guardrails and deny-lists apply to this agent regardless of the current run?
Which agentic threats (memory poisoning, goal manipulation, tool misuse and related ASI items) have been assessed for this agent, and which mitigations are in force?
How are policy refusals, unauthorised function requests and internal failures represented, and who is notified?
Which skills does this agent advertise, and what identifiers, tags and examples describe each skill?
Where did each skill originate (first-party, registry, third-party pack), and which version is pinned?
Which skills are public, which appear only on an extended card, and which principals may invoke each skill?
Which tools and resources are bound to this agent, and what names, titles, descriptions and schemas define them?
For each tool, is user consent required before invocation, and are tool annotations treated as untrusted?
What validation, rate limits, timeouts, output sanitization and audit logging are required for tool calls by this agent?
May the tool list change over time, and how are list-changed notifications handled without per-connection variance except by authorization?
Which working, episodic and long-term memory stores does this agent use, and what integrity or isolation controls protect them against poisoning?
Does scaffolding provide context-compression or unbounded-horizon memory, and what stopping condition still applies?
How long may each memory class be retained, and who may inspect, correct or erase it?
Is internal memory hidden from peer agents under opaque execution, and which summaries if any may be exported?
What is this agent's current platform lifecycle state, and on which agent platform does that state apply?
Which lifecycle transitions are allowed from the current state, and which actors (agent versus AMS) may initiate each transition?
At what event time did the current state begin, and at what observation or ingestion time was that transition recorded?
In the current state, does the message transport buffer, forward or reject inbound messages?
Is this agent registered with its home AMS, and which ams-agent-description (name, ownership, state) is stored?
Which Directory Facilitators hold a description of this agent, and when does each registration lease expire or renew?
What search constraints, access restrictions and exception codes apply when other agents look up this agent?
Which scaffolding pattern or pre-built agent product turns the backing model into this agent, and which tools does that scaffolding expose?
What standing budget and stopping condition limit this agent's runtime (tokens, wall-clock, step count), and who may raise the budget?
What residual registrations, mandates, tools, memory and credentials must be removed when the agent is destroyed or quits, and who attests completeness?
Which AI system exposes this agent, and is the agent required to exist only inside that system?
Which person or organisation owns this agent, and are additional owners recorded?
Which prompt or agent-configuration artifacts does this agent currently use?
Which peer agents may this agent discover, delegate to or refuse, and is internal state shared with them?
Which inter-agent and tool protocols does this agent speak, and which protocol versions are declared?
How does this agent mint or accept conversation, context and message identifiers so concurrent dialogues stay distinct?
Does this agent refuse to expose internal plans, memory or tool implementations to A2A peers while still exposing MCP tools to its host?
In which jurisdictions or processing locations may this agent run or persist data, given EU territorial scope for AI systems used in the Union?
Who is the provider and who is the deployer of the AI system that exposes this agent, and who is the FIPA owner?
Who may read, modify, suspend or destroy this agent record at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scope, and which actions are refused as unauthorised?
Which management actions, tool consents and authority changes must be audited, and for how long?
When and how is the agent record, memory, directory entry and mandate deleted or anonymised, including after lease expiry or destroy?
Which inference, scaffolding and task settings were used in the latest evaluation of this agent, and are they sufficient to reproduce the result?
What quality, safety or threat-coverage claims are made for this agent, and which artefacts or probe results support them?
What validation status does this agent currently hold (unevaluated, draft, passed, failed, waived), and who attested it?
Who created or imported this agent record, from which source system, and at what event versus ingestion times?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
